scope: Read-only source/API/official documentation review. No production edits, Python generator execution, Gradle, compiler, ADB, VM or external writes by this reviewer.

finding.source_module: OpenCC data/scripts/common.py imported by the bridge generator and reverse.py
finding.current_generate_inputs: All source files excluding Git metadata include generated __pycache__/common.*.pyc.
finding.current_install_inputs: @InputDirectory data includes all generated Python caches.
finding.risk: Cold first generation can add a task input during execution, so next no-change build reruns; fixture prewarming may hide it. Different Python cache tags or added/removed local caches can cause unnecessary deployment/resource checksum task work.

minimum_complete_fix: Filter **/__pycache__/** and **/*.pyc from both producer and install semantic source file inputs, not producer only. Keep actual .py scripts/data/CMake/native source covered.

For install: keep inputDir as @Internal directory location and expose a RELATIVE @InputFiles FileTree with matching cache exclusions; this mirrors the producer pattern without execution-time Project access.
Set PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 on both host configure and host build ExecOperations, so Python launched under official CMake inherits it.
Add -B before the script path in direct install python3 argv. Do not edit pinned OpenCC sources or implement a replacement conversion algorithm.

stronger_semantic_input_boundary.important_distinction: -B/PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE prevents writing caches; it does not disable reading existing valid source-tree pyc. Excluding pyc from Gradle inputs alone therefore does not prove arbitrary pre-existing bytecode can never affect execution.
stronger_semantic_input_boundary.optional_if_claiming_source_tree_caches_: Set PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX (Python>=3.8) to an owned fresh build/temporary directory for both host and direct Python execution, together with no-write behavior. Python documents that source-tree __pycache__ is then ignored. Keep the prefix outside source and clear its owned tree when execution starts.
stronger_semantic_input_boundary.claim_limit_without_prefix: Say caches are ignored for Gradle invalidation and no new cache is written, not that arbitrary existing valid bytecode can never be loaded.

necessary_execution_gates: Record exact original cache files/bytes before test, preserving any original evidence.

Start from a genuinely cold isolated source without __pycache__/pyc (or relocate original caches to an evidence directory and restore afterward). Run actual generate/install/checksums; verify bridge bytes and no new source-tree cache artifacts.
Repeat unchanged task request and require all3 UP-TO-DATE with no task action events.
Add/change/remove an ignored source-tree cache file and require UP-TO-DATE; inspect task action-start inputFiles to prove cache paths excluded from both task inputs.
Continue harmless .py script mutation/fresh host build, failure-blocking, exact source restoration and final clean-source successful build gates. Real .py source must still invalidate.
Do not reuse old prewarmed cache test/old CI as proof of corrected cold behavior; retain them as historical scoped results.
